title: Part C: ceramah & pengumuman — kalimat pertama adalah topik
title_target: Talks and lectures — topic, structure, and details
goal: Mengikuti monolog dua–tiga menit tanpa mencatat: memegang topik dari kalimat pertama, menghitung poin lewat penanda urutan, menangkap angka dan nama yang muncul di pilihan jawaban, dan menjawab soal tentang instruksi di bagian penutup.
bekal: menyebut topik ceramah setelah mendengar satu kalimat
mengenali penanda urutan (first, another, however, finally) sebagai batas antar-soal
menjawab soal 'why does the speaker mention X' dari fungsi kalimatnya, bukan isinya

sections.title: Part C: tiga monolog, satu suara, tidak ada yang mengulang

blocks.text: Part C adalah bagian terakhir Listening: **tiga monolog** sepanjang 1,5–2,5 menit, masing-masing diikuti 3–5 soal, total **11–13 soal** (nomor 39 sampai 50). Tiga monolog itu hampir selalu tiga jenis yang sama: satu **pengumuman atau tur** (orientasi mahasiswa baru, panduan museum, pengumuman di awal kelas), satu **kuliah sains** (biologi, geologi, astronomi), dan satu **kuliah sejarah atau ilmu sosial** — biasanya sejarah Amerika.

Aturannya sama dengan Part B: audio sekali, **tidak boleh mencatat**, dan pertanyaan tidak tercetak. Bedanya, di sini tidak ada lawan bicara yang bertanya balik atau mengulang. Dosen berbicara terus dari kalimat pertama sampai penutup, dan tidak seorang pun akan berkata *sorry, when was that again?* untukmu.

Yang mengimbangi: monolog TOEFL ITP sangat **rapi**. Ia ditulis untuk tes, bukan direkam dari kelas sungguhan, sehingga strukturnya jauh lebih teratur daripada kuliah asli. Kalau kamu hafal strukturnya, kamu tahu di mana tiap jawaban akan muncul sebelum audio menyala — dan itulah isi unit ini.

blocks.title: Cara memakai unit ini
items: Audio Part C ada di menu **Simulasi**. Di unit ini kamu berlatih dengan transkrip, dengan aturan yang sama: baca sekali, jangan mengulang.

Untuk tiap transkrip: (1) baca pilihan jawaban empat soalnya di Latihan; (2) baca transkrip satu kali dari atas ke bawah; (3) jawab. Jangan membaca transkrip dua kali walaupun ragu — keraguan itulah yang sedang dilatih.
Setelah selesai, cek pembahasan bukan hanya untuk soal yang salah. Untuk tiap soal, tanyakan: jawabannya ada di bagian mana monolog — pembuka, tubuh, atau penutup?

sections.title: Pola monolog TOEFL: pembuka, tubuh, penutup

blocks.text: Hampir semua monolog Part C dibangun dari tiga bagian yang sama, dan soalnya mengikuti urutan bagian itu.

head: Bagian
Isinya
Bunyinya
Soal yang lahir dari sini
rows: Pembuka (1–2 kalimat)
Topik, dan sering peta isi
*Today I want to talk about the Pony Express… · I want to cover three questions: how far they go, how they find their way, and how they fuel the trip.*
Soal pertama: *What is the talk mainly about? · What is the purpose of the announcement?*
Tubuh (3–4 poin)
Satu poin per paragraf, tiap poin dibuka penanda
*First… · Second… · Another… · The most extreme example… · However… · For example…*
Soal-soal tengah, satu per poin, dalam urutan yang sama
Penutup (1–2 kalimat)
Tugas, instruksi, atau langkah berikutnya
*For Thursday, read chapter twelve… · Tomorrow at ten there's a mandatory meeting… · All right, follow me.*
Soal terakhir: *What will the students probably do next? · What are the listeners asked to do?*

blocks.text: Kalimat pertama adalah **topik**, dan itu bukan kiasan. Penulis soal TOEFL tidak membuka ceramah dengan lelucon atau cerita pribadi; kalimat pertama menyebut subjeknya dengan kata benda yang jelas, dan soal *main topic* menanyakan kata benda itu. Kalau kamu melamun di lima detik pertama, kamu kehilangan soal yang paling mudah di seluruh section.

Penanda urutan adalah **pembatas soal**. Begitu dosen berkata *second* atau *another thing*, jawaban untuk soal sebelumnya sudah lewat, dan bagian untuk soal berikutnya dimulai. Pakai kata-kata itu untuk menggerakkan matamu ke soal berikutnya — persis seperti penanda pindah bagian di Part B.

items: **Urutan**: *first, second, third, finally, the last thing, one more thing* — batas antar-poin.
**Tambahan**: *another, also, in addition, on top of that* — poin baru dalam kelompok yang sama.
**Kontras**: *however, but, on the other hand, what they do not rely on is…* — sering tempat pengecoh: hal yang disebut sebelum *however* biasanya bukan jawaban.
**Contoh**: *for example, for instance, the record holder is…, the most extreme example…* — contoh biasanya jadi bahan soal *why does the speaker mention…*.
**Penutup**: *for next week, before we go, one last thing, don't forget* — instruksi yang jadi soal terakhir.

head: Jenis soal
Bunyinya
Cara menjawabnya
rows: Main topic
*What is the talk mainly about? · What is the main subject of the lecture?*
Kalimat pertama. Pengecoh favorit: sub-topik yang dibahas panjang di tengah (*the Arctic tern*) dan topik yang terlalu luas (*birds*).
Purpose
*What is the purpose of the announcement? · Why is the speaker talking to the students?*
Untuk pengumuman, tujuannya biasanya disebut langsung (*I want to go over three things*). Jawaban yang benar mencakup seluruh monolog, bukan satu poin saja.
Detail
*According to the speaker, how far…? · What does the speaker say about…?*
Satu poin di tubuh monolog; pilihan memuat angka atau nama yang persis diucapkan, plus dua–tiga angka lain dari kalimat tetangganya.
Why does the speaker mention X?
*Why does the speaker mention the North Star? · Why does the speaker talk about riders' weight?*
Jawabannya adalah **fungsi**: memberi contoh, menjelaskan sebab, menunjukkan betapa pentingnya sesuatu. Pilihan yang cuma mengulang isi X biasanya pengecoh.
What will the listeners probably do?
*What will the students do before the next class? · What will happen tomorrow at ten?*
Penutup. Jawabannya adalah instruksi yang diucapkan terakhir, bukan kegiatan yang disebut di tengah monolog.

blocks.text: Jenis keempat — *why does the speaker mention* — yang paling sering salah, karena pilihannya semua terdengar benar secara isi. Kuncinya: jangan tanya 'apa yang dikatakan tentang X', tanya '**untuk apa** X disebut'. Kalau X datang sesudah *for example*, fungsinya memberi contoh. Kalau sesudah *because* atau *I've seen…*, fungsinya alasan. Kalau X adalah angka yang ekstrem, fungsinya menunjukkan betapa besar atau betapa penting.

Ini keluhan paling umum soal Part C: 'ada lima angka dan saya tidak boleh menulis'. Betul, dan itu memang disengaja. Tapi kamu tidak perlu mengingat lima angka. Kamu hanya perlu mengenali **satu** angka yang ada di pilihan jawaban ketika ia diucapkan.

blocks.title: Empat cara memegang angka & nama tanpa pensil
items: **Pilihan jawaban adalah catatannya.** Sebelum audio menyala, kamu sudah tahu soal 41 menawarkan *every fifteen minutes*, *every thirty minutes*, *every hour*. Tugasmu bukan mengingat jadwal shuttle, tapi menunggu salah satu dari frasa itu diucapkan. Begitu terdengar, jawab di kepala dan tinggalkan.

**Angka yang diralat: ambil yang terakhir.** *Take the seven-thirty shuttle, not the seven forty-five.* Dua angka dalam satu kalimat; kata *not* menentukan yang mana. Di kuliah bentuknya *you'll see the figure ten quoted — it's actually three*.

**Nama: ingat fungsinya, bukan bunyinya.** Kamu tidak akan diminta mengeja *Waddell*. Kamu akan ditanya apa yang dilakukan tiga orang itu (mendirikan perusahaan) atau apa yang terjadi di *St. Joseph* (titik awal rute). Saat nama disebut, tempelkan satu kata fungsi padanya.

**Ulangi dalam hati, sekali.** Angka yang diulang dalam hati satu kali bertahan sekitar 20 detik — cukup, karena soal untuk angka itu datang segera sesudah monolognya selesai, bukan di akhir section, dan pilihan jawabannya ada di depan matamu.

blocks.text: Pengumuman pendek di awal praktikum. Tabel di bawahnya membedah empat soal yang bisa ditulis dari tiga puluh detik ini — perhatikan bahwa soal pertama lahir dari kalimat pertama, soal terakhir dari kalimat terakhir.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: Before we start today's experiment, three quick things about the lab. First, safety goggles stay on the whole time you're in this room — not just while you're handling chemicals. I've seen too many people take them off to write and then get splashed. Second, anything that produces a vapor goes under the fume hoods along the back wall. If you're not sure whether something produces a vapor, assume it does. And third, a change to the syllabus: your lab notebooks are due at the end of today's session, not next Monday. I want to give you feedback before the second experiment. All right, pick up your materials at the front bench.

head: Soal
Jawaban
Pengecoh & alasan
rows: What is the announcement mainly about?
Rules and a deadline for the laboratory
Kalimat pertama: *three quick things about the lab.* Pengecoh *the results of an experiment* — kata *experiment* ada, tapi belum ada hasil apa pun.
When must students wear goggles?
Whenever they are in the laboratory
*the whole time you're in this room — not just while you're handling chemicals.* Pengecoh *only when handling chemicals* adalah persis yang ditolak sesudah *not just*.
Why does the professor mention people getting splashed?
To explain why goggles must not be removed
Fungsi kalimat itu adalah alasan (*I've seen too many people…*). Pengecoh *to describe an accident in a previous class* mengulang isinya, bukan fungsinya.
When are the lab notebooks due?
At the end of today's session
*due at the end of today's session, not next Monday.* Pengecoh *next Monday* adalah tanggal lama yang diralat — dan kata *syllabus* memancing peserta memilihnya.

blocks.text: Tiga puluh detik, empat soal, dan empat-empatnya mengikuti urutan monolog: pembuka, poin pertama, alasan poin pertama, poin ketiga. Monolog Part C yang sesungguhnya lima kali lebih panjang, tapi jalannya sama.

Berhenti di sini. Buka **Latihan 1**, baca pilihan jawaban empat soalnya, lalu baca Talk 1 **satu kali, tanpa mengulang**, dan jawab. Ulangi untuk Talk 2 dengan Latihan 2, dan Talk 3 dengan Latihan 3. Tiap monolog kira-kira dua menit dalam kecepatan bicara normal.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Hadley College. My name is Renee, I'm a junior here, and for the next hour I'll be your guide for the campus tour. Before we start walking, I want to go over three things: your ID card, the shuttle system, and where you can eat.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: First, your student ID. If you haven't picked yours up yet, the card office is in the basement of the student center, and it's open until six tonight. Don't put it off — the card is your library card, your meal card, and the key to your residence hall. Without it, you can't get into your own building after ten p.m. There's a twenty-five-dollar fee to replace a lost card, so put it somewhere safe.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Second, the shuttle. Hadley has two campuses — this one, the main campus, and the science campus about a mile and a half north. The blue shuttle runs between them every fifteen minutes from seven in the morning until eleven at night on weekdays. On weekends it runs every half hour, and it stops at nine. The shuttle is free; you just show your ID. If you have an eight o'clock lab at the science campus, take the seven-thirty shuttle, not the seven forty-five — the later one is always full.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Third, food. Your meal plan works at the main dining hall, which is the brick building behind me, and at the café in the library. The dining hall serves breakfast from seven, and the last dinner seating is at eight. The library café is open until midnight during the semester, which many of you will discover during finals week.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: One last thing before we go. Tomorrow at ten there's a mandatory meeting for all first-year students in Bartlett Auditorium. Your academic advisors will hand out your course schedules there. If you miss it, you'll have to make an individual appointment, and those fill up fast. All right — follow me, and watch the steps.

blocks.title: Talk 2: Biology lecture on bird migration

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: Today we'll look at bird migration, and specifically at how birds manage journeys that would kill most other animals. I want to cover three questions: how far they go, how they find their way, and how they fuel the trip.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: First, distance. The record holder is the Arctic tern, a small seabird that weighs about as much as a bar of soap. It nests in the Arctic during the northern summer, then flies to the edge of Antarctica for the southern summer, and comes back. Tracking studies show a round trip of roughly forty-four thousand miles a year. Over a lifetime of thirty years, that adds up to the distance to the Moon and back — three times.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: Second, navigation. Migrating birds use several compasses at once. Day fliers use the sun. Night fliers use the stars — young birds actually learn the pattern of the night sky around the North Star before their first trip, by watching it rotate. And most species, as far as we can tell, sense the Earth's magnetic field, which gives them a direction even under heavy cloud. What they do not rely on is memory of the landscape. A young bird flying alone for the first time has no landscape to remember.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: Third, fuel. Before departure, a migrating bird eats until it has nearly doubled its body weight, and almost all of that extra weight is fat. The most extreme example is the bar-tailed godwit, a shorebird that flies from Alaska to New Zealand — about seven thousand miles — without landing once, in roughly eight days. To make room for the fat, the godwit actually shrinks its own digestive organs before it leaves, since it won't be eating anyway.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: For Thursday, read chapter twelve, and come with one question about the godwit study, because we'll spend the first half of class on it.

blocks.title: Talk 3: History lecture on the Pony Express

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: Today I want to talk about the Pony Express, which lasted only eighteen months but became one of the most famous businesses in American history.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: In 1860, a letter from the East Coast to California went by stagecoach along a southern route and took about three weeks — or by ship around South America, which took even longer. Three freight businessmen, William Russell, Alexander Majors, and William Waddell, believed they could do it in ten days using riders on horseback. Their route ran nearly two thousand miles, from St. Joseph, Missouri, the western end of the railroad and the telegraph, to Sacramento, California. The first riders left both ends on April third, 1860.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: The system worked like a relay. About one hundred and ninety stations were built along the route, roughly ten to fifteen miles apart, which was as far as a horse could gallop at full speed. A rider changed horses at each station, taking only two minutes, and rode seventy-five to a hundred miles before handing the mail to the next rider. The mail traveled in a leather cover called a mochila, which fit over the saddle and could be moved to a fresh horse in seconds. Riders were young and light — the company wanted men under one hundred and twenty-five pounds — because every extra pound slowed the horse.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: Was it a success? As a delivery service, yes: in eighteen months, only one mail pouch was ever lost. As a business, no. Sending a half-ounce letter cost five dollars at first, an enormous sum, and even after the price fell to one dollar, the company lost money on every run. What actually finished it was technology. On October twenty-fourth, 1861, the transcontinental telegraph line was completed, and a message could cross the continent in minutes. The Pony Express announced it was closing two days later.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: For next week, read the chapter on the telegraph, and think about this question: why does a business that failed so quickly remain so famous?

Jawaban

rows: B

Kalimat pembuka: *I want to go over three things: your ID card, the shuttle system, and where you can eat* — tiga layanan kampus. (A) terlalu sempit: asrama cuma disebut sekilas soal kunci. (D) memakai *course schedules* dari penutup, tapi pembicara hanya menyebut pembagian jadwal, bukan membantu memilih. (C) tidak dibahas.
C

*Without it, you can't get into your own building after ten p.m.* (B) memelintir *twenty-five-dollar fee to replace a lost card* — biayanya untuk kartu hilang, bukan terlambat mengambil. (A) bertentangan: kantor buka *until six tonight*, tidak ada yang bilang tutup seminggu. (D) tidak disebut.
A

*every fifteen minutes from seven in the morning until eleven at night on weekdays.* (B) *every half hour* adalah jadwal **akhir pekan** — pengecoh klasik: angka benar, hari salah. (C) dan (D) tidak disebut. Perhatikan: pilihan jawaban sudah memuat *fifteen* dan *thirty*, jadi kamu hanya perlu menunggu kata *weekdays*.
D

Penutup: *Tomorrow at ten there's a mandatory meeting… Your academic advisors will hand out your course schedules there.* (C) memakai *six tonight*, bukan besok jam sepuluh. (A) kafe perpustakaan buka sampai tengah malam — tidak ada jam buka. (B) tur berlanjut **sekarang** (*follow me*), bukan besok.
A

Kalimat pertama: *how birds manage journeys that would kill most other animals* = bertahan dalam migrasi panjang; peta isinya (jarak, navigasi, bahan bakar) menegaskan itu. (B) *tracking studies* memang disebut, tapi hanya sebagai sumber angka. (C) tidak dibahas — dosen tidak pernah menjelaskan **mengapa** burung bermigrasi. (D) terlalu sempit: makan dibahas hanya sebagai persiapan terbang.

B

(A) bertentangan — justru medan magnet bumi yang bekerja *even under heavy cloud*. (C) dan (D) tidak disebut; (D) masuk akal di dunia nyata, tapi dosen tidak pernah membandingkan dengan pelaut.

A

(B) bertentangan: rel kereta berakhir di *St. Joseph, Missouri, the western end of the railroad*. (A) *young* tidak sama dengan *teenagers*, dan itu isi, bukan fungsi. (B) dan (D) tidak disebut.

blocks.title: Yang perlu dicatat dari tiga monolog ini
items: Tiga soal pertama tiap monolog (1, 5, 9) dan tiga soal terakhirnya (4, 8, 12) semuanya dijawab dari **kalimat pembuka** dan **kalimat penutup**. Itu enam dari dua belas soal — separuh Part C — yang bisa kamu amankan hanya dengan hadir penuh di sepuluh detik pertama dan sepuluh detik terakhir tiap monolog.

Soal 3, 6, dan 11 adalah soal angka, dan ketiganya memakai pengecoh yang sama: **angka benar untuk subjek yang salah** (*every half hour* untuk akhir pekan, *thirty years* untuk umur, *ten to fifteen miles* untuk jarak antar-stasiun). Yang perlu kamu pegang bukan angkanya saja, tapi angka + satu kata subjeknya: *fifteen-weekdays*, *forty-four-miles*, *seventy-five-rider*.

Soal 7 dan 10 (*why does the speaker mention…*) sama-sama punya pengecoh yang **benar isinya** tapi salah fungsinya (*most riders were teenagers*, *to compare birds with early sailors*). Sebelum memilih, ulangi dalam hati kalimat tepat sebelum atau sesudah X: kalau ada *because*, jawabannya alasan; kalau ada *the most extreme example*, jawabannya contoh.
